x: Eric Bishop kept this position on the next stage and then Eddie Short lost one more place to Jim Peters of Essex Beagles and although Bill Lucas took us back into 3rd position our final runner Vern Blowfield found he could not make any impression on Jimmy Wood and Tommy Rowe who were in front of him.

Incidentally, Jim Peters of Essex Beagles, the A.A.A. Marathon champion set up a new course record of 15 mins. 22 secs., which was 13 seconds inside the old figures set up by Bill Lucas in last year's race.
Jim Peters was the next runner for Essex Beagles on the long 7th relay, and seeing that he broke the course record, it was not surprising that he gained ground from Len Herbert.

In the Senior race over 10 miles there was a field of 371 starters and after the usual fast start, Gordon Pirie and Frank Sando were out on their own, with Dennis Holden also in complete isolation in third place. Jack Brown was running quite well and was only beaten by the three above mentioned, plus Jim Peters and R.
The actual race was won by Jim Peters in the amazing time of 2hrs. 40.2secs., and in the Southern Team Race we were 6th, and also 6th in the "Sam Ferris Cup."
The second annual race was held at Wimbledon on June 27th, and we had received a good entry, which comprised most of the leading road men, with the exception of Jim Peters and Stan Cox.

However even Driver's time was not unbeatable, for first Jim Peters lowered it by 10 seconds and in doing so passed Charlie Walker and took Essex Beagles into 2nd place, and later by Alec Olney who reduced it by another 7 seconds without bringing his club T.V.H. anywhere near the front.

Continuing along his road of success Jack Brown sliced off 41 seconds from Jim Peters course record, a most meritorious performance. The race seemed to resolve itself quite rapidly into two fierce battles, between O'Gorman, Brown, Keily, Hicks, Lambert and Haslam on the one hand and a close bunch of…
10 Stage.Len Bishop(21.16) If Len could have kept up the pace he showed over the first mile we would have wiped out Jim Peters' name from the book, and Belgrave would have moved out of sixth place.

However, the main part of the season is yet to come and he should find some tough cross-country races a valuable background to his road-running, as have Jack Holden, Jim Peters and Fred Norris before him!

On the next leg T.V.H. pulled out their trump card in the form of Mike Wiggs who with a great run knocked off 10 secs. from Jim Peters's stage record set in 1953 and this time in turn was bettered by Bruce Tulloh running in the lead position who ran even 30 secs. faster than Wiggs.
This might be a reason why no Englishman has ever been successful in the race, the highest placing being second by Jim Peters in 1954, beaten by Finland's Veikko Karvonen.
Incidentally, the main team trophy is named after one of the marathon "greats" - Jim Peters. Laurie once again had a recall to the table for the Vet's Prize.

Jim Peters emerged with a win in the 6 miles having not yet moved up to the marathon distance. The AAA were followed by the first International match of the season against France at the White City, in which we surprisingly won by 72 to 57 points with Sydney Wooderson producing yet another classic 3…
That man Zatopek again turned out as a novice in the marathon and proceeded to trounce the world's best by over 2½ minutes despite a brave attempt by Jim Peters to run everybody into the ground.
In the Poly Marathon there was "an amazing time" by Jim Peters and our team was led home by Geoff Pearson and Arthur Whitehead to finish 6th.

As a matter of interest, Jim Peters won the above Windsor to Chiswick marathon in the then world's best time of 2 hrs 18 mins 40.2 secs. At this time, interest in road running was increasing and in 1952 the Road Runners Club was formed.
